speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you have an unspecified dermatological condition; please describe the lesions you are experiencing, including their size, color, and how long they have been present. Also, have you noticed any itching, bleeding, or changes in their appearance recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 62-year-old male. The patient has recently immigrated to the US from Africa and seeks evaluation for a non-healing, red, crusty lesion on the shaft of his penis and a similar lesion on his left middle finger. Previous treatments in his home country for syphilis and eczema have been unsuccessful. The patient is a smoker, with a history of two packs per day for the last 30 years.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Squamous cell carcinoma of the penis and finger (secondary to chronic scarring or smoking). The patient's history of failed syphilis/eczema treatment, combined with the specific description of non-healing, crusty lesions on high-risk sites (penile shaft, finger) in a heavy smoker, strongly suggests malignancy. Given the high probability of cancer, immediate biopsy of both lesions is indicated.
